pr_body:
Fixes #2914 regression

When there are only `response` schema set, the AJV validation instance is wrongly built, even if not necessary.
So the AJV root instance is not created and the shared cache:

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/aad7d7ea216d5a367335b3dbbadaee2c3291a78c/lib/schema-compilers.js#L38

trigger the error.

(I'm still figuring out how this issue has been introduced after the v3.12)

pr_comments:
This issue is quite funny 😂

I would like to explain:
there are 3 contexts in place:
1. the root context
2. the first register
3. the second register

The root loads and does not create any schema validator compiler, because it is not necessary: there are not any routes!

The second context loads and it needs a schema validator, so it builds it because the root one does not exists.
(NOTE: it is not necessary the validator, since there are not body, params headers and query schemas tbh, so this PR fix this behaviour)
The second context build the serializer too and `fast-json-stringify` mutates the external schemas

The third context loads and it needs a schema validator compiler too, so it builds it.. and crash because the schemas are mutated!

So, as funny workaround for this issue, it is necessary to register a route in the root context:

```
fastify.get('/', {
  handler () {},
  schema: {
    body: S.ref('ListSchema#')
  }
})

fastify.register(
  async (app) => { app.get('/resource/', routeResponseSchemas, () => ({})) },
  { prefix: '/prefix1' }
)
fastify.register(
  async (app) => { app.get('/resource/', routeResponseSchemas, () => ({})) },
  { prefix: '/prefix2' }
)
```

This will trigger the optimization to have only one AJV instance when the schemas are always the same 😄

Anyway, FIXES are coming 👍 

What is not totally clear to me, is: why previous versions of fastify have not this issue because this optimization was already in place - I would like to deeper into this
It's still not clear to me why each context needs its own schema container.
Do you mean in general or in this case?
In general. But it seems to apply directly to this case.

> In general. But it seems to apply directly to this case.

In this case, a validator is not needed at all, so this PR will fix this behaviour (and bump the `fast-json-stringify` to fix the issue)

In general: every context with at least one route that uses schemas needs a validator and/or a serializer.
An encapsulated context uses the validator and/or a serializer:

1. owned by the parent context if and only if: it exists and the user doesn't add new shared schema (aka `fastify.addSchema()` - this explain the `addedSchemas` flag:

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/76b1b1406982644e11d0093a1d539e821756f0fe/lib/schema-controller.js#L33 

2. or the context builds its own validator/serializer (so children contexts will inherit the new ones and repeat the logic)


----

I have checked the "why" of this is a regression:
before there where this statement:

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/2755/files#diff-47b0948ab224d4db8f374686960e631b9a6497c073ac72097afb05d8ba130c31L126-L131

that was cloning the shared schemas **every time**, and now it is just a reference to the same schemas (this change was inspired by [this comment](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/2755#discussion_r549049444) tho)
For this reason, the `fast-json-stringify` behaviour was not shown up.

> Is this shippable?

I think it is

> @jsumners ?

Sure. I'm not fully clear on it, but I consider @Eomm the expert on this stuff.
This pull request has been automatically locked since there has not been any recent activity after it was closed. Please open a new issue for related bugs.
